6. Sessions: London + NY killzones.

not_validated.name: ICT Core (sweep → displacement/MSS → FVG entry)
rules: 1. HTF bias: H4 close[1] vs H4 EMA(50) — above = bullish, below = bearish.
2. Sweep: M15 bar takes out a confirmed swing pool and CLOSES back inside it.
3. Displacement: body >= 1.0 x ATR(14), closing in bias direction.
4. MSS: close[1] breaks the intervening swing in bias direction.
5. Entry: limit at the 50% level of the displacement-leg FVG.
6. Stop: beyond the sweep extreme + 0.25 x ATR.
7. Target: next opposing liquidity pool; reject setup if RR < 2.0.
8. Sessions: London 07:00-10:00 and NY 12:00-15:00 UTC only.

methodology_notes.compounding_artifact: total_pnl / final_balance COMPOUND position size off a growing balance with fractional units and no liquidity cap. For high-frequency models this explodes: turtle_soup/DE30 reports $57.8M from $10k, which is arithmetic, not a forecast. Use expectancy_R and fixed_size_pnl for a realistic read — the same model at FIXED $75 risk/trade returns ~$84k over 8 years.
methodology_notes.sharpe_frequency_bias: The shared gate FAILs any model with per-trade Sharpe < 0.5. That is an extraordinarily high bar — mean P&L half a standard deviation PER TRADE — which essentially no real strategy meets, and it penalises high-frequency models that accumulate edge across many small trades. sharpe_annualised (per-trade Sharpe x sqrt(trades/yr)) is reported alongside: turtle_soup scores 2.4-2.8 annualised while failing the per-trade test. The gate was NOT changed after seeing these results — moving a threshold to make things pass is how backtests get talked into deployment. Flagged for Jase.

headline: 0 of 28 model/instrument combinations cleared the gate. Nothing is marked deployable. turtle_soup is the only model with both a large sample and consistent multi-year profitability, but it fails the per-trade Sharpe test — see methodology_notes.
